newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on USDA crop reports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on USDA crop reports.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on bearish input from USDA's September crop report and supply/demand data, traders said.
A sharp drop in wheat futures also hit the market, they said.
"We're all over the place. They're getting in and getting out," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

USDA early Wednesday said the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 8.804 billion bushels, above USDA's forecast in August for 8.695 billion. But the latest government outlook was below an average of analysts' estimates of 8.857 billion.
The government also increased to 668 million bushels its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. corn ending stocks from the previous outlook for 523 million.
While the government reports were given a bearish slant many traders said there remains the possibility of continued volatile corn futures trading.
Lagging maturity of the U.S. corn crop and forecasts for cool weather to soon move into the U.S. Midwest kept alive some bullish ideas, the traders said.
Corn closed one to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down five at $3.60-3/4.
Key sellers were Goldenberg Hehmeyer with 10 million bushels of December and Cargill Investor Services with four million bushels of December, the traders said.
ADM Investor Services bought 4.5 million bushels of March, Cargill Inc bought 4.0 million December and Continental Grain bought two million December, the traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 53,000 contracts, up from 45,510 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

Corn options trading featured Smith Barney with 2,000 bought in the March $3.60 calls and 2,000 March $3.20 puts sold at even money, the traders said. LFG Inc bought 1,000 December $3.10 puts at 5-1/2 cents, they said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, down from 28,198 Tuesday.
